claims.source_quote_ar: هذا النداء والخطاب ليسا على ظاهرهما
claims.claim_ar: النداء «يا أيها الذين آمنوا» ليس ظاهريًا بل خطاب عام/تذكير عام مقصود لجميع الأزمنة والرسل، أي تحويل المخاطَب الظاهري إلى عمومية في المعنى.
claims.claim_en: The vocative 'O you who believe' is not merely literal here but functions as a general/collective address — a rhetorical shift making the command applicable across times (i.e., a general admonition rather than a time-bound call).

claims.source_quote_ar: وصف اللَّه شدّة شكيمة اليهود وصعوبة إجابتهم إلى الحق
claims.claim_ar: الآية تقرِن اليهودَ والنصارى وتعرضهما بشكلٍ متوازيٍ متباين لتأكيد حالة العداء والجمود لدى اليهود مقابل ميل بعض النصارى؛ هذه مقابلة بلاغية تُبرز الفارق في الاستجابة.
claims.claim_en: The verse presents Jews and Christians in juxtaposition/parallel, emphasizing the Jews' firmness in rejection and contrasting it with the relative pliability of some Christians; this parallelism (muqabalah) heightens the contrast and the warning.
claims.needs_review_reason: The supporting chunk comments on the characterization of Jews and Christians in tafsir (parallel contrast), but does not quote the exact Qur'anic phrase from this ayah; inference links the tafsir observation to the ayah's wording.

claims.source_quote_ar: وتكريره هذا القول مراراً مصداق لما ذكره الزمخشري
claims.claim_ar: التركيب المتكرر «أَوْلِيَاءَ بَعْضُهُمْ أَوْلِيَاءُ بَعْضٍ» يعمل كتكرار وتأطير بلاغي (توكيد وتحذير) يضخم المعنى التحذيري من التولِّي.
claims.claim_en: The doubled/parallel formulation 'allies one of them are allies of another' functions as repetition/parallelism — an emphatic device that intensifies the warning against taking them as allies.
claims.needs_review_reason: The cited tafsir passage explicitly notes rhetorical repetition elsewhere; applying 'takrar' to this ayah is plausible but the chunk does not directly analyze this exact phrase, so the linkage is inferential.

warnings: Source chunks supplied are tafsir excerpts (primarily al-Kashshaf and Tabari). They discuss rhetorical matters but are not the named rhetorical theorists (al-Jurjani, al-Sakkaki, al-Baqillani, al-Suyuti). Where claims are inferred from general tafsir commentary rather than explicit balagha labelling, confidence is lowered and marked in needs_review_reason.

Some claims (muqabalah, takrar) map tafsir observations onto classical rhetorical categories; reviewers should verify labeling (e.g., whether commentators themselves described these devices with the same technical terms).
